prologue.speaker: anna
prologue.text: I know, I know. Stupid question. You're always here.

prologue.speaker: anna
prologue.text: I'm sorry you have to… watch all of this through my eyes. Especially today. Everything's a little blurry here, in case you haven't noticed. Literally — right now I feel like I'm looking at the world through two lenses at once, and neither one is in focus.

prologue.speaker: anna
prologue.text: Do you know how many people are walking the streets of this country right now who shouldn't be? Not because of a miscarriage of justice — not the case where an innocent man goes down, they at least make movies about that. I mean the opposite. The ones who are guilty, a hundred percent, and still sleep in their own bed tonight instead of a cell. Because there wasn't enough evidence. Because the lawyer was smarter than the prosecutor. Because someone in the interrogation room couldn't find the right words in the twenty-four hours they had — and then they send him in, polite, in a suit, and he says: 'my client declines to answer questions.'

prologue.speaker: anna
prologue.text: The system loves to pretend that's a bug. The cost of due process, you know. I think it's a feature. It's designed exactly so that scum can slip between your fingers if it knows the right words — or stays quiet long enough. And the worst part is you don't have to be a genius to do it. You just have to hold out. Not crack. The system will give up before he does.

prologue.speaker: anna
prologue.text: Well, I don't give up. Maybe that's the one thing I'm truly good at — not letting go. While everyone else is looking for a balance between the rights of the suspect and justice, I find the words. I always find them. Because somewhere behind the door of every interrogation room there isn't an abstraction, not 'the defense' — there's some Edward who drowned a child in a pool and has already rehearsed how he'll spread his hands in court. And the only thing standing between him and the next pool is me, and whatever I can pull out of him in a few hours, while there's no lawyer around to teach him how to keep quiet.

prologue.speaker: anna
prologue.text: All right. Enough philosophy. I've got a new case, and my head is splitting like there's someone in there conducting an interrogation too — not a very polite one, I have to say. Help me pull myself together. You always did.

epilogue.speaker: weller
epilogue.text: First degree. He'll get the maximum. You did it, Crawford.

epilogue.speaker: anna
epilogue.text: It worked. He'll go away for life. So why don't I feel better? Used to be I'd feel better at this point. At least for a couple of hours.

window.speaker: anna
window.text: The sun is so bright this morning. My eyes hurt...

water.speaker: anna
water.text: I really want to chat with someone by the water cooler, but there's no time for that now.

clock.speaker: anna
clock.text: As long as I can remember, this clock has always run a little fast or a little slow.

lockers.speaker: anna
lockers.text: Metal lockers. Other people's coats, other people's lives.

notice.speaker: anna
notice.text: The notice board. Here's shift schedules and stuff.

duty.speaker: anna
duty.text: The duty post. A visitor log, cold tea, a radio tuned to three stations at once.

vending.speaker: anna
vending.text: Okay, Anna, repeat after me... I don't want chips. Chips are bad for your health. I don't want chips...

sink.speaker: anna
sink.text: I've probably been working too much lately. My face looks tired. Should probably use more foundation.

sofa.speaker: anna
sofa.text: Great, our old sagging, fart-stained sofa.

int1_table.speaker: anna
int1_table.text: The strict interrogation room. It's uncomfortable, but that's the point.

int2_table.speaker: anna
int2_table.text: The soft interrogation room. Armchairs, a floor lamp, a water jug. Cozy — just enough for a man to forget where he is.

fire_escape.speaker: anna
fire_escape.text: The fire escape. It reeks of tobacco. From here you can see the yard, where nobody ever walks.
